exposure: maternal inflammatory bowel disorder (IBD) during pregnancy
cohort: Live births in Finland between 1996 and 2014 were included and followed up until December 2018.
finding: Offspring exposed to maternal Crohn's disease during pregnancy had modestly higher risks of early sleeping, continence, and feeding disturbances, and a higher risk of dispensed antipsychotic, anxiolytic, hypnotic, and/or sedative medications.
mod_finding: The associations between maternal Crohn's disease exposure and offspring outcomes were not explained by cesarean section.
